summary: CC registered a struct tag only after parsing its body and allocated a fresh type on definition, so self-referential members (struct block_header *next) and forward-declared tags (typedef struct ast_node ast_node_t before the definition) failed to resolve.
evidence: self-referential structs ... the struct's own tag only gets registered into the symbol table *after* its body is parsed

summary: CC's parser had no switch/case/default support at all, so vm.c's bytecode dispatch loop and lexer.c failed to parse.
evidence: `switch`/`case` isn't implemented in CC's parser at all — a real, substantial gap

summary: CC's parameter-list parser did not handle function-pointer parameters of the form TYPE (*name)(PARAMS), so script/parser.c and compiler/parser.c failed to parse.
evidence: FAIL kernel/lang/compiler/parser.c: cc: kernel/lang/compiler/parser.c:130: unexpected token (near '?')

summary: CC's initializer parser did not support designated initializers, so eval.c's VAL_ZERO = { VAL_INT, { .i = 0 } } failed to parse; worked around by rewriting it positionally in the kernel source.
evidence: `VAL_ZERO`'s designated initializer (`{ .i = 0 }`) is a real gap — CC's initializer parser has no support for designated initializers at all.

summary: CC declared ND_COMMA but never implemented the comma operator in parser or codegen, so for-loop increments like `pn = pn->next, i++` failed to parse.
evidence: `ND_COMMA` was declared but never actually implemented anywhere — the comma operator (`pn->next, i++` in a for-loop increment) simply doesn't parse.

summary: The new self-hosted Makefile referenced $(BUILD) in := assignments before BUILD was defined.
evidence: Right, `BUILD` needs to be defined before it's referenced with `:=`.

summary: AS lacked the 32-bit register-indirect forms of lidt/lgdt (e.g. lidt [ecx] emitted by CC's builtins); lgdt only had the hardcoded 16-bit disp16 form.
evidence: as: line 148: unsupported instruction form: lidt

summary: CC codegen only supported brace-init lists for globals; local aggregate initializers like `exec_result_t r = { EXEC_NORMAL, VAL_ZERO };` failed to compile.
evidence: local (stack) variables ARE brace-initialized in this codebase (`exec_result_t r = { EXEC_NORMAL, VAL_ZERO };`), contrary to the existing assumption that only globals use brace-init

summary: CC's emit_data_bytes had no struct/union path for global .data initializers, silently emitting wrong bytes for brace-initialized struct globals.
evidence: properly implement struct-initializer support for both the global `.data` path (which has a silent-corruption bug, not just a crash)

summary: CC marked per-file generated labels __str_N and __static_N as global, so linking several translation units hit duplicate-symbol errors.
The Makefile did not make compiled objects depend on the CC/AS binaries, so after rebuilding CC, stale .o files were reused and the old duplicate-symbol error came back until make clean.
evidence: Stale objects — Make doesn't track that `CC`'s own source changed. Let me force a clean rebuild.

summary: CC gave extern variable declarations (extern uint32_t isr_stub_table[32];) their own .bss/.data storage and never emitted an `extern NAME` directive for them, which AS requires for undefined symbols.
evidence: `extern` variable declarations get treated as real definitions, allocating their own `.bss`/`.data` storage instead of just referencing the symbol defined elsewhere

summary: CC's earlier walk_collect dedup fix nulled n->next while recursing, which cut off prog's chain during the is_local scan, so forward-referenced functions defined later in the file (parse_statement) were wrongly declared extern.
evidence: temporarily nulling `n->next` before recursing) corrupts `prog`'s chain *while it's being scanned* by `is_local`'s check

summary: AS's far-jump encoder always emitted a 16-bit offset, so in 32-bit code `jmp 0x08:label` in gdt_flush was 2 bytes short, which caused a GPF and then a triple fault at boot.
evidence: the far-jump encoder always writes a 16-bit offset (`e16`), but in 32-bit mode the `EA` far-jump instruction needs a 32-bit offset — it's 2 bytes short

summary: CC's walk_collect treated indirect calls through function-pointer variables (tinyfs.c's block_read(...)) as calls to extern functions and emitted a spurious `extern block_read`.
evidence: with indirect calls (my earlier fix), the callee can be a variable — it spuriously emits `extern block_read` even though `block_read` gets a real local definition later

summary: CC's parse_global_var always set external linkage, so file-scope static variables (block_read/block_write in tinyfs.c) were emitted as global symbols.
evidence: `parse_global_var` unconditionally sets `n->is_global = 1` regardless of the `static` keyword — every file-scope `static` variable ... gets external linkage

summary: With the self-built kernel, the tinyfs superblock magic read at mount came back with its high 16 bits corrupted (0x0d805331 instead of 0x54465331), so execution took a wild jump to EIP 0x3 (#UD, vector 6). The disk image held the correct bytes. The root cause (in/out ax,dx missing the 0x66 prefix in AS) was not found by the end of the chunk.
evidence: `eax = 0x0d805331` but should be `0x54465331` — the low 16 bits are right, high 16 bits are corrupted.
